paragraphs.text: This is [Anhua dark tea](anhua-dark:definition), a protected origin name, from the mountain county of [Anhua](anhua:where-it-is) on the Zi river in north-central Hunan. The county sits at the northern foot of the Xuefeng mountains. Most of it is hills and steep valleys, ground where rice is hard to grow and tea does well. The leaf grows in warm, wet air, and the tea is piled and kept in that same air. That is why the trade ties [the finished tea to the place](anhua:why-people-value-it) and not only to the method.

Every Anhua tea begins as [heimaocha](anhua-dark:making). Large Anhua leaf is fixed, rolled, piled, rolled again and dried. Like any [dark tea](dark:definition), it keeps changing after it is made, as warmth, moisture and microbes slowly darken and mellow the leaf.
Made in 2024, this tea is two years into that change. Anhua tea is [kept for years](anhua-dark:ageing) and is said to improve, though no agreed number of years marks it as aged.

brewing.text: In a small pot or gaiwan, use water at the boil and start with a steep of about 15 to 30 seconds, a little longer each round. Pressed and aged Anhua tea is also commonly simmered in a pot.

notice.text: Pine smoke or pine resin above all, a sweet taste and aftertaste, and a mellow, thick, smooth cup; a liquor from yellow and orange to orange-red. Young tea is often smokier in the first infusions and a little bitter, sweetening as the infusions go on.
